_note: Kling 3.0 Pro, silent, 16:9. Each clip runs start frame -> end frame. Image IDs are Higgsfield job IDs (generated stills) or media IDs (uploaded frames).
style: Silent. Photoreal, 35mm documentary film look, fine grain, smooth constant camera speed, no shake, no cuts. Muted palette, warm lamp-black shadows, no bright green. No text, no logos, no faces, no lens flares, no floating particles.

shots.prompt: One continuous slow shot. The camera glides forward and gently down through the misty understory of an old Kerala forest, passing between ferns and buttress roots toward a single shaft of low golden sunlight, and settles at plant height on a young holy basil plant standing in the beam. Dust moves only inside the light.

Almost still macro, slow push-in. A weathered hand enters slowly from the right into the shaft of light, gently takes one holy basil leaf between thumb and forefinger and lifts it a little toward the camera; the plant stays soft behind. Natural, unhurried movement, correct fingers.

Very slow push-in. The leaf is raised against the low sun until it fills the frame; it becomes fully backlit, the hand and the forest fall away into warm black, and the vein network glows translucent gold. One continuous move.

One continuous macro move. The glowing gold veins of the leaf slowly dim and harden into dark incised grooves; the leaf tissue becomes the dry honey-coloured fibres of a palm-leaf manuscript strip, and the branching veins straighten into rows of soot-darkened stylus marks. The camera drifts slowly to the right along the strip toward its binding hole. Gradual physical transformation. The marks stay soft and never form legible letters.

The camera pulls slowly back and up from the palm-leaf strip, revealing it is one leaf in a bound bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts held between wooden boards and tied with a cotton cord, resting on dark rosewood and lit by a small brass oil lamp at the right. The flame flickers gently. Smooth constant pull-back, ending still, with the left of the frame dark.

Locked camera. The cotton cord binding the manuscript bundle begins to glow with warm gold light from within, then slowly lifts free of the bundle as a single fine golden thread and rises out of the top of the frame, while the lamp dims and the whole frame fades to complete darkness.

One continuous move. Low over still golden oil with slow concentric ripples, the camera rises and tilts down until it looks straight down, revealing the oil fills a wide bronze uruli vessel; herb roots and dark leaves sink slowly at its edges and the oil simmers gently with fine rings on its surface.

Continuous move. The camera drifts from the bronze vessel to follow a smooth, unbroken golden stream of the finished oil pouring through a fine white cotton cloth into a plain unlabelled amber glass bottle on dark wood. Slow and calm, warm side light.

The camera rises slowly straight up above the bottle until it looks directly down; warm light grows, the dark table brightens into a calm ivory surface, and the single circle of golden oil multiplies into a perfectly regular grid of identical two-piece hard capsules, opaque and matte, with amber-brown caps and cream bodies, filling the frame. Smooth and exact.

Slow, smooth descent. From the grid of identical softgels the camera settles onto a single capsule resting at the centre of the polished steel pan of a precision balance in a clean ivory and glass enclosure; cool soft daylight with a warm rim on the capsule. Everything settles to stillness.

The camera rises slowly away from the balance into soft bright morning light; the frame washes to warm ivory, and out of the light a single fine thread of real gold draws itself in one gentle curve across ivory handmade paper. Ends still and quiet.
